title: A prime over a principal ideal in a local normalization contains a height-one prime over it
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its field of fractions and $N\subseteq K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume $R$ is local, meaning it has a unique maximal ideal. For every $0\ne b\in N$ and every prime ideal $P\subset N$ containing $b$, there exists a height-one prime ideal $Q\subseteq P$ of $N$ containing $b$. Here a height-one prime is a nonzero prime with no prime strictly between it and $(0)$. No Noetherianity hypothesis on $N$ is imposed.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules. Theorem 4.10.5 proof, printed p. 91 (PDF p. 105), paragraph beginning We next prove that for any non-zero element b: the principal-height refinement subclaim, proved using Lemma 4.8.4, contraction of integral closures of principal ideals, and the Dimension Inequality B.2.5. It precedes and does not assume the final height-one intersection assertion. Author-hosted PDF read online at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $0\ne b\in N$ and a prime $P\subset N$ containing $b$. Put $S=R[b]\subseteq N$. This is a domain inside $K$, and its fraction field is $K$: it contains $R$, so every fraction of elements of $R$ is a fraction of elements of $S$, while every fraction of elements of $S\subseteq K$ lies in $K$. The evaluation map $R[T]\to S$, $T\mapsto b$, is surjective, so $S$ is of finite type over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Moreover $S$ is integral over $R$, since each of its elements belongs to the integral closure $N$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; adjoining b is the enlargement used after Lemma 4.8.4 in the proof of Swanson–Huneke Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 91.

proof.text: The integral closure of $S$ in $K$ is again $N$. Indeed, an element integral over $R$ satisfies the same monic equation over $S$, giving one inclusion. Conversely, let $x\in K$ be integral over $S$. The algebra $S[x]$ is generated by the integral element $x$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] makes it finite over $S$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes it integral over $S$. Together with the integrality of $S/R$ from Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] makes $S[x]$ integral over $R$. In particular $x$ belongs to $N$.

source.place: Tags 02JJ, 00GK and 00GN: finite integral generators, finite implies integral, and transitivity of integrality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normalization-finite-local-model] with base domain $S$, its fraction field $K$, its normalization $N$ from Step 2, and the chosen prime $P$. Its hypotheses require a Noetherian domain, not locality of the base, so Step 1 suffices. Obtain $S\subseteq C\subseteq N$ and $p=P\cap C$ such that $A=C_p$ is a Noetherian local domain and $B=N_P$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $K$. Since $b\in S\subseteq C$ and $b\in P$, its image lies in $pA$. The element $b$ remains nonzero in $A\subseteq K$. The inclusion $A\subseteq B\subseteq K$ is injective and integral by the integral-closure clause.

source.place: Lemma 4.8.4, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 99), applied over R[b]; compare the enlargement by b in the principal-height paragraph of Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 91 (PDF p. 105). Author-hosted PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] in $A$ to $I=bA$ and the maximal prime $pA$. Obtain a prime $q\subseteq pA$ minimal over $bA$. The prime $\bar q=q/bA$ in $A/bA$ has height zero: a strictly smaller prime would pull back to a prime strictly below $q$ containing $bA$, contrary to minimality. Here inverse images are prime directly from the product test modulo $bA$, and the surjective quotient map recovers each ideal from its inverse image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with ring $A$, $t=1$, $f_1=b$, $J=bA$ and $\mathfrak P=q$. It gives $\operatorname{ht}q\le\operatorname{ht}\bar q+1=1$. Since $b\ne0$ lies in $q$ and $A$ is a domain, $(0)\subsetneq q$ is a strict prime chain; thus $\operatorname{ht}q=1$.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology (4), and Tag 00KW, lemma-one-equation (the cited height-quotient node states its height form).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] applied to the injective integral inclusion $A\subseteq B$ from Step 3, choose a prime $Q^{*}\subset B$ contracting to $q$. It contains the image of $b$, since $b\in q$. Every strict chain of primes of $B$ below $Q^{*}$ contracts to a strict chain of primes of $A$ below $q$: contractions are prime by the product test, and strictness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability]. Therefore $\operatorname{ht}Q^{*}\le\operatorname{ht}q=1$.

source.place: Tags 00GQ and 00GT, lemma-integral-overring-surjective and lemma-integral-no-inclusion. This chain argument replaces the dimension-inequality step in the source subclaim.

proof.text: Use clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] for $N\to B=N_P$ and the multiplicative subset $N\setminus P$. The inverse image $Q$ of $Q^{*}$ is prime and disjoint from $N\setminus P$, hence $Q\subseteq P$; it contains $b$ and is nonzero. Every prime below $Q$ is also disjoint from $N\setminus P$ and hence extends to a prime of $B$. Extension and contraction are inverse by that clause and preserve inclusions by their definitions. Consequently a strict prime chain below $Q$ extends to a strict chain below $Q^{*}$ (strictness follows by contracting back). Thus $\operatorname{ht}Q\le1$. Since $N$ is a domain and $Q$ contains $0\ne b$, the chain $(0)\subsetneq Q$ shows that $Q$ is a height-one prime containing $b$ and lying in $P$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization, prime correspondence and its explicit inverse. No Noetherianity of N is used.

proof_origin.place: The principal-height subclaim in the proof of Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 91 (PDF p. 105), and finite-local-model Lemma 4.8.4, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 99). Independent expansion: replace the base by R[b], apply the existing finite-local-model statement, then use the Noetherian principal height bound, lying over, incomparability and localization prime correspondence. The author-hosted PDF was read online; local PDF WANTED.
